cards.text: Amos, a shepherd from Tekoa, sees visions about Israel (Amos 1:1). In his last one, the LORD said the end had come for His people Israel (Amos 8:2). Now the prophet says, “I saw the Lord standing beside the altar, and He said:”

cards.question: Standing beside the altar, the Lord gives an order about the pillars. What does He say to do to their tops?

answers.text: Strike them so the thresholds shake
Wash them so the altar stays clean
Coat them so the gold shines bright

cards.text: And then those pillars come DOWN. The Lord says to topple them on the heads of all the people, and He will kill the rest with the sword.

cards.question: The Lord says a few of the people who flee will get away.

cards.text: Then the Lord goes through every hiding spot there is, starting at the bottom. “Though they dig down to Sheol, from there My hand will take them;”

cards.question: Digging down to Sheol won't work. So what does the Lord say He'll do if they climb up to heaven?

answers.text: Leave them up there for good

cards.text: Hide on top of Carmel, and the Lord says He'll track them there and seize them. Down low, up high, MOUNTAINTOP, friend, this is the worst game of hide-and-seek anybody ever played.

cards.question: If they hide from the Lord at the bottom of the sea, He'll command the ___ to bite them.

cards.text: Even captivity won't hide them. If their enemies drive them off as captives, the Lord says He'll command the sword to slay them there.

cards.question: The Lord says He will fix His eyes on them for good and not for harm.

cards.text: Now Amos tells who's behind all this: the Lord GOD of Hosts, who touches the earth and it melts, and all who live on it mourn. I touch a hot oven door one time and I'M the one who melts.

cards.question: When the Lord GOD of Hosts touches it, all the land rises like the ___, then sinks like the river of Egypt.

cards.text: Amos keeps going: “He builds His upper rooms in the heavens and founds His vault upon the earth.” Meanwhile it takes me ALL afternoon to build one gingerbread house, and the roof still caves in.

cards.question: The Lord GOD of Hosts summons something and pours it over the face of the earth. What is it?

cards.text: Amos wraps it up: “The LORD is His name.” Then the LORD asks Israel about the Cushites, the people of Cush, the land south of Egypt (Ezekiel 29:10): “Are you not like the Cushites to Me, O children of Israel?”

cards.question: The LORD reminds Israel that He brought them up from Egypt. Who does He say He brought up from Caphtor?

cards.text: And the Arameans? The LORD says He brought them up from Kir. Then He says His eyes are on the sinful kingdom, and He will destroy it from the face of the earth.

cards.question: The LORD says He will utterly destroy the house of Jacob.

cards.text: Then the LORD says He'll shake the house of Israel as grain is sifted in a sieve, but not a pebble will reach the ground. I know a sieve, friend: I sifted so much flour once my mustache came out WHITE for a week.

cards.question: Where does the LORD say He'll shake the house of Israel like grain in a sieve?

answers.text: Along the banks of the Jordan

cards.text: Last line, and it's a sharp one. The LORD says all the sinners among His people will die by the sword.

cards.question: Which sinners among His people does the LORD point to?

answers.text: Those who say disaster will never reach them
Those who say the LORD has gone silent
Those who say the prophets are lying

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates stop 2. Four of its six choice cards (cards 4, 6, 10 and 12) are multiple choice, with only one fill in the blank (card 2) and one true or false (card 8).

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The joke calls the Lord hunting people down to kill them "the worst game of hide-and-seek anybody ever played." That makes deadly judgment into a game, and it doesn't treat the people's situation (fleeing for their lives) with respect.

rule.text: Humor about people in Bible stories looks at their human situation with respect.

findings.problem: The card says Cush is "the land south of Egypt (Ezekiel 29:10)." Ezekiel 29:10 only says "as far as the border of Cush." It never says south, so the reference doesn't support the fact as stated. Word it from what the verse says, like "the land past Egypt's border."

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The Arameans show up here, and the Philistines on card 6, with no simple word on who they are. The Cushites were introduced on card 5, so the three groups are handled unevenly.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: Everything before this card points to True. Stop 1 says none will escape, and card 7 says the kingdom will be destroyed from the face of the earth. Nothing hints at the turn in verse 8 ("Yet I will not utterly destroy"), so a thoughtful baker reasons their way to the wrong answer and can only get it right by luck. This is the passage's key turn. The story card should set up that a turn is coming, without giving the answer away.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.
